I'd put a footnote briefly defining "gravitational lensing", since I imagine most readers won't know what that is.

with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED]

item.title: The Black Hourglass: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
+Overall Thoughts
– hide block

Overall, I thought it was alright. You were worried about your dialogue, but it seemed fine to me (however, I'm not the best with dialogue, so you should definitely get a second opinion).

My first main concern is that you didn't cite your image. First, check the image use guidelines and make sure that your image is CC compliant. If it is, put a license box at the bottom of the page. If it isn't, you can't use it in your article. If you want to know where to find CC compliant images, I would recommend Wikimedia Commons and CCSearch.

My second issue are the test logs. The focus of your is on Licht's character arc, but your logs are pretty detached from that. You can also cut down on the description of SCP-####-A through -I by having there only be one button that lets Licht move outside of the flow of time, and then just letting him walk around outside of time instead of using multiple other buttons to do so.

+line-by-line
– hide block

SCP-#### has the ability to create a temporal anomaly capable of consuming the time of macroscopic life

"consuming time" is pretty vague. You explain the effect of this later in the paragraph, but I think you should find a better descriptor for the SCP's effect.

The activation time is inconsistent, along with the amount of time SCP-#### consumes.

I'd change this to "Both the activation time and the amount of time SCP-#### consumes1 are inconsistent."

SCP-#### appears to be designed to permanently attach itself to an humanoid individual. The requirements for this process to occur are as of yet unknown. It is also unknown if it is possible to remove SCP-#### without physically damaging the individual which it has attached to.

This makes it sound like SCP-#### is physically attached to an individual, when the recovery log shows that it just floats near them.

extreme gravitational lensing

I'd put a footnote briefly defining "gravitational lensing", since I imagine most readers won't know what that is (or maybe everyone knows what that is and it's just me).

it has been designated SCP-####-2

I'd change it to SCP-####-1 since you never mentioned -1.

with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED]

I don't understand why this is redacted. I'd recommend reading this guide

I just happen to be in the wrong place

You don't need to change this since dialogue doesn't have to have perfect grammar, but "happen" should be "happened"

Subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####. Immediately, SCP-#### began activating, and subject disappeared from the cell.

I'd change this to "SCP-#### activated immediately after subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####." You can remove "subject disappeared from the cell" because the next couple sentences imply that the subject disappeared.

Subject 6 was found to have transported to a closed doorway, and suffered [DATA EXPUNGED]. Subject died █ minutes after initial recovery.

I'd change this to "Subject 6 was found to have been transported inside of a closed doorway and could not be recovered." Saying that they couldn't be recovered implies that they were located but died before they could be properly rescued.

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM

I'm not going to do an LBL on this just now because I have a queue to get through - if you'd like one let me know and I can try and do one next week.

I enjoyed this. There is a really… uncomfortable sense to the progression here. On some level, I feel genuinely a little gross about reading the story of this person's suffering, knowing what will happen the whole way through, and just having it happen without being able to do anything about it. That being said, it's the kind of uncomfortable and gross that works, I think, largely because of the fact that it's clearly framed as such.

I've considered saying that the ending is a little flat, but I don't think there's a solid way to change that which wouldn't also make the article overall feel just a bit too uncomfortable? I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. The ending is a little less climactic than it could be, I think, but it's not bad. Like WarFang said, it's a relief to see Lief is okay, and that might be enough on its own.

I think the voice constructed for Lief could be a little more… distinct? It's not bad, but it doesn't feel particularly unique and given the emotional and narrative core of the article is built around those diary entries, and therefore Lief's voice, it could do with being a bit more compelling in my opinion. Give the reader more to latch onto, and it will make the overall arc even more involving and engaging.

Otherwise, I think this is a solid piece of writing. Well done, and I wish you the best of luck with it.

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: The Friendly Shadow: Re: The Friendly Shadow
item.content:encoded:
You have definitely made some improvements, but there are still some issues here and there.

> Line by line < 
hide

Special Containment Procedures

Update: Following incident XXXX-A2, SCP-XXXX-1 has been provided with counseling and further educational within Site-17.

I would list the date the update occurred here and fix some spelling, and phrasing:1

Update: Following incident XXXX-A2, SCP-XXXX-1 has been provided with weekly counselling and a high-school education within Site-17.

Description

Update_Incident_XXXX-A2:SCP-XXXX-2 is a painting showing a silhouetted humanoid figure standing on a hill. Further information is limited to personnel above level 3 clearance.

Space needed between XXXX-A2: and SCP-XXXX-2. I also don't see the point of the lines between the words there. It could just be 'Update Incident XXXX-A2.

Discovery

3ed

should be

3rd

Addendum XXXX.

Mabye this should be called Addendum XXXX.1? It seems to make more sense to me.

Interview XXXX.1

It should be noted that SCP-XXXX is referred as "Thomas" by SCP-XXXX.

Would be phrased better as

It should be noted that SCP-XXXX-1 reffers to SCP-XXXX by the name "Thomas".

SCP-XXXX-1: "I knew he was in the Museum. I broke him inside in the first place."

Dr. Rose: "And what influenced you to break into the Museum?"

SCP-XXXX-1: "I was scared Thomas was stuck inside, he hadn’t come out in hours."

This seems weird to me. Dr Rose asks why he broke him inside in the first place, then -1 answers that he was already in there? Because Dr Rose doesn't bring him up on the discrepancy, I'd assume this wasn't intentional.

+ 'LEVEL 3 CLEARANCE REQUIRED - INPUT CREDENTIALS'

This should follow all of the following text (except for the navigator), as a government document wouldn't just redact one thing that can be discovered anyway with context clues. Also it probably shouldn't have the inverted commas around it.

> Overall < 
hide

While a lot of the spelling has been cleaned up, I think the article still suffers from some of the broader issues I pointed out earlier. For one, I think the article could benefit from an Image of either SCP-XXXX-1 or SCP-XXXX in order to break up the text.

I still think the experiment logs detract from the story and are kind of unnecessary. As I said before; this would be more interesting to me if we saw some more characterisation of SCP-XXXX-1 and SCP-XXXX, which could be used in place of the experimentation. Again, this is all my opinion, and I have not got any writing on the site, so take it with a grain of salt.

I think the most important thing this article is in need of is more characterisation because at this point the ending note just doesn't hit for me.

Feel free to PM me again if you make any changes to the article.

Footnotes
1. I'll just put the corrections underneath, as the crossing out and underlining makes everything feel cluttered.

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
drops in time 4 thoughts

+ smells like brain
- thonk

Preface: I am a trans person, but it goes without saying that my own thoughts don't stand for the whole, and I'd still recommend seeking out more willing trans/nb critters.

Okay SO, I read the first(?) iteration of this originally about a week+ back, and I can definitely say that some of my original opinions have changed for this article.

At first - and this was very much a more personal gripe, mind you - I really wasn't…feeling it, y'know? It was a pretty solid draft but initially it wasn't necessarily to my tastes.

This is no longer much the case, though.

The addition of the diary excerpts definitely makes this, for me - it's a perfect touch of a human element I didn't realise that the original iteration was lacking. The slow creep of dread and anguish that you build up through it is, truth be told, viscerally uncomfortable but in the way that's reflective of good, solid writing - as a transmasc person specifically I felt that shit in my soul.
(Moreover the fact Leif was okay and this wasn't gonna end up being a more tragic example of the anomaly's effect was a huge relief tbh)

I still do hold this worry about this anomalisation of the concept of dysphoria, in the context of trans and nb people, though perhaps a little less now. Moreover I did not think my stance on that would change, but lo, here we are.

I don't think I really have much negative to say beyond the personal concerns I've laid out abane this paragraph. You took a solid working draft and you made it into a good draft, in my opinion, capturing perfectly the reality and horror of what it's like to deal with dysphoria. Furthermore, it doesn't feel like the article is forcing the idea that dysphoria has to be to particular severity.

I look forward to seeing where this goes. It certainly is interesting.

item.title: The London Brick Incident: 2nd Draft: Re: The London Brick Incident: 2nd Draft
item.content:encoded:
I have read through your draft and want to share my critique.

Open critique
– hide block

The first and most important point is that it is too long. You want to share a lot of information, which shows that you really thought of a lot of details, but it affects the readability of your draft. You should focus more on the main information that you want to share. There is less room for imagination and interpretation which are a big part of how someone experiences your article.

You have shown that you are capable of using some rather unique words to describe some effects/situations which is great, but hold yourself a bit back.

Please remove the [REDACTED] and █ in your article. It especially distracts you from getting intrigued by the interview. The interview seems promising but I think you need to work on Captain Myers dialogue a bit. The Doctor seems calm, direct which I appreciate and I think serves as an opposite for Myers. I am not very good in interviews myself but Myers comes over a bit off in my opinion. I can't describe it better than, sorry.

The autopsy really shows that you did some homework. For example the microscopic image of red blood cells with spores around them is actually a pretty realistic description. Other things like including the epidermis and cerebellum was nice. I liked the autopsy the most of all the addenda.

About the discovery, it really took me by surprise at the end, I recommend that you put this before the addenda or something. It can also help with setting the tone for the coming story that you want to tell.

Generally I like what you are going for. The idea is good, the way you brought that idea over lacked a bit of structure. Keep it a bit more constrained, focus on the main aspects. One thing I learned from being here is that an SCP with lots of content does not need to be an SCP with a lot of text.

item.title: The London Brick Incident: 2nd Draft: Re: The London Brick Incident: 2nd Draft
item.content:encoded:
Hey Sybert6000. I'll be critiquing the London Brick Incident for you.

+ Critique
– hide block
  • Narrative.

The narrative, and by proxy, the anomaly is too complicated and the article itself is far, far too long. Instead of adding complexities to the article to lengthen the narrative, you should be adding depth. Depth is a far more intriguing way to explore an article as it will allow you to explore the nuances and important details of your article rather than adding more information. Less is more in a horror-themed article.

  • Tone and language.

The tone and language used in the article is lacking at times. This is especially notable in your interview logs. Examples include:

We checked the corporal, he was dead, like I said the head was probably caved in when he was hit, I ordered my men back when one of my men called out "Captain more of them, they're moving they're moving!".

Fuck me it was like fighting off an army of bulldozers, I wouldn't even say three minutes passed before they were at the front door, at that point four men are fuck all against an army of scuffed Mr potato heads.

The Captain has just gone from callously describing the death of the men under his command to referring to instances of an unknown lifeform as Mr. Potato Heads. There's a massive clash of tone there.

More importantly than either of these, however, the article shows more than it tells. You don't need to describe in detail how the Foundation came to work out how the brick monsters came about, you should be showing this to us. The horror of an article is best left to the imagination of the reader.

Redaction should go. It has no place in the article and only detracts from the tone.

  • The anomaly.

A good anomaly is simple but deep. This is an extremely convoluted and complex anomaly that lacks any real depth. I'd strip back the extraneous elements of the anomaly and focus on the core.

I was especially intrigued by the idea that it was made on accident by the Brick Company attempting to cut corners in the brick-making process. This is something you could explore in more depth.

  • Overall.

I love the idea. Brick fungus monsters are cool and pretty terrifying. However, the execution leaves something to be desired in the finished product. The autopsy report is definitely the best part of the article and there's lots of information that you've put in the description that can be moved there.

Always remember that a narrative has a beginning, middle, and end. You want to move the reader through each stage by increasing the tension, drama, or horror with each and every single sentence. Here, the autopsy should act as your middle by heightening the horror and tension.
